question: P, Q, R and S are four points on a circle. PR and QS intersect at a point X such that ∠QXR = 120° and ∠XRS = 10°. The measure of ∠QPR is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In ΔSXR, the exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

⇒ ∠QXR = ∠XSR + ∠XRS

⇒ 120° = ∠XSR + 10° ⇒ ∠XSR = 110°

Angles subtended by the same arc (QR) in the same segment of a circle are equal.

⇒ ∠QPR = ∠QSR = ∠XSR = 110°

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ∠QXR = 120°

⇒ ∠XRS = 10°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Linear pair sum = 180°

⇒ Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

⇒ Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.
